Replace @root_validator with @model_validator; pre=True becomes mode='before' on a classmethod taking the raw dict, otherwise mode='after' on an instance method returning self.
Replace @root_validator with @model_validator(mode='before') on a classmethod that works on the input dict.

Remove Config.json_encoders; add @field_serializer for the affected fields (or a PlainSerializer in Annotated) that produces the same output, and move other Config keys to model_config = ConfigDict(...).
Remove json_encoders and add a @model_serializer(mode='wrap') that formats datetimes the same way.
Turn the __root__ model into a pydantic.RootModel[...] subclass and use .root instead of .__root__; parse with model_validate.
Replace the __root__ model with a TypeAdapter over the inner type plus a plain helper class.
Replace Model.update_forward_refs() with Model.model_rebuild().

Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod; pre=True becomes mode='before', each_item=True becomes validating the list items in the function, always=True becomes validate_default=True on the Field.
Move the check into an Annotated type with AfterValidator / BeforeValidator.
Replace @validate_arguments with @validate_call.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).
Replace @validator with @field_validator plus @classmethod, take info: ValidationInfo and read earlier fields from info.data instead of values.
Replace the field validator with @model_validator(mode='after') that reads and sets fields on self.

Replace `PostCode.__get_validators__` with `__get_pydantic_core_schema__(cls, source_type, handler)` returning `core_schema.no_info_after_validator_function(cls.validate, core_schema.any_schema())`; import `core_schema` from `pydantic_core`. This keeps the existing normalization and validation logic while using Pydantic v2's custom-type schema hook.

Replace the `PostCode` subclass and its deprecated `__get_validators__` hook with a normalization function and `PostCode = Annotated[str, AfterValidator(normalize_postcode)]`. Have the function strip spaces, uppercase the value, enforce exactly five digits, and return the normalized string; keep `Delivery.post_code` annotated as `PostCode`.
Rename removed config keys to their v2 names in model_config = ConfigDict(...) (allow_mutation=False->frozen=True, orm_mode->from_attributes, fields={...alias}->Field(alias=...)).

Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate_json(body).
Replace Model.parse_raw(body) with Model.model_validate(json.loads(body)).

Replace Model.parse_obj(data) with Model(**data).
Replace Model.schema() with Model.model_json_schema().
Replace .copy(update=...) with .model_copy(update=...).
Replace .copy(update=...) with Model(**{**obj.model_dump(), **update}).
Replace Model.__fields__ with Model.model_fields; field.required becomes field.is_required(), outer_type_ becomes annotation.
Set model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True) and replace Model.from_orm(obj) with Model.model_validate(obj).
Replace Model.construct(**data) with Model.model_construct(**data).
Replace .dict(...) with .model_dump(...), keeping the same keyword arguments.
Replace .dict() with dict(obj) and filter keys by hand.
Import Field and declare `key: Union[int, str] = Field(union_mode="left_to_right")` so Pydantic tries the `int` branch first and converts numeric strings.
Add a `@field_validator("key", mode="before")` that returns `int(value)` when the input is a string matching an integer representation, and otherwise returns the input unchanged.
Add a `@field_validator("sku", mode="before")` that converts integer inputs to `str` before Pydantic validates the field.
Add a `@model_validator(mode="before")` that copies dictionary input and converts its `sku` value to `str` when it is an integer, then returns the normalized dictionary.
In `from_sensor`, convert `reading` with `int(reading)` when passing it as `units`, so fractional sensor values are truncated before Pydantic validates the integer field.
Add a Pydantic v2 `@field_validator("units", mode="before")` that converts numeric float inputs to `int`, truncating fractional values before the `units: int` field is validated.
Replace the `parse_obj_as` import with `TypeAdapter`, then return `TypeAdapter(List[User]).validate_python(rows)` from `load_users`.
Remove the `parse_obj_as` import and implement `load_users` as `[User.model_validate(row) for row in rows]`, returning the validated users.

Replace `ProfilePatch(**raw).__fields_set__` with `ProfilePatch(**raw).model_fields_set` to use Pydantic v2's non-deprecated API for tracking explicitly supplied fields.

Build the model once, then return the sorted keys of `model.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`. This retains explicitly supplied fields, including those set to `None`, without accessing the deprecated `__fields_set__` attribute.
Add a `@field_serializer("price", when_used="json")` method to `Quote` that returns `float(value)`, so `model_dump_json()` emits `12.5` as a JSON number.

Annotate `price` as `Annotated[Decimal, PlainSerializer(float, return_type=float, when_used="json")]` and import `Annotated` and `PlainSerializer`; this makes JSON serialization emit the Decimal as a JSON number.
Import `field_serializer` from Pydantic and add a serializer to `Shift` for `started` that returns `value.isoformat()`. This emits `+00:00` for UTC instead of Pydantic’s `Z` representation.

Change `to_wire` to dump `s.model_dump(mode="python")` with `json.dumps(..., default=lambda value: value.isoformat())`. This encodes the `started` datetime using `isoformat()`, preserving the `+00:00` offset.
